Metadata.title: HUET — LIBRAS data infrastructure
Metadata.description: An initiative in development focused on linguistic data infrastructure for LIBRAS, research and new technological possibilities.

Home.title: Data infrastructure
Home.description: Language lives in movement, space and the connections between people. We aim to build a foundation of linguistic data that opens new possibilities for research and technology.
Home.sectionTitle: Language at the centre. Research as our path.
Home.sectionBody: HUET begins with the intention of organising and documenting linguistic data for LIBRAS, Brazilian Sign Language. Our vision is to support research and future applications in artificial intelligence, computer vision and technologies related to sign languages.
Home.challengeTitle: How do you document a conversation that unfolds in space?
Home.challengeBody: In Brazilian Sign Language, hands, facial expressions and body movements work together to convey meaning. To study a conversation later, it helps to know who is signing, whom they are addressing and what came before.
Home.proposalBody: We aim to organise LIBRAS recordings so researchers can find relevant material and understand how it was produced. Three questions guide our planning.
Home.recordBody: Consider the interaction itself and the information people will need to interpret it.
Home.describeBody: Explore ways to connect each excerpt with observations about the language used.
Home.consultBody: Plan ways to locate recordings and learn how they may be used.
Home.linguisticsExample: When someone returns to an earlier part of a story, how do they indicate whom they mean? Comparing excerpts from different narratives could help researchers describe the role of gaze and space in those references.
Home.visionExample: When a hand passes in front of the face, which movements can a camera follow? Recordings described by people familiar with LIBRAS could help researchers identify where a tracking system loses the movement.
Home.aiExample: Could a model find other passages where someone asks a question? Comparing the results with descriptions by signers could show which cues the model picks up and which it misses.
Home.sectionNote: We are in the planning and development stage. The infrastructure and its potential applications are part of this vision for the future.
Home.applicationsIntro: A collection of LIBRAS recordings described in context could help researchers explore questions like these.
Home.aboutTitle: A Brazilian initiative in the planning stage
Home.aboutBody: The name HUET refers to Huet’s place in the history of deaf education in Brazil. The initiative grew out of an interest in documenting LIBRAS and supporting people who study the language.
